description: C++ CONSUMER half of the skill-chains feature: teach SkillTooltipStore to reconstruct a whole skill chain and teach the OCR emit path to render EVERY tooltip in the chain (each translated, in chain order) instead of only the single identified skill. When a matched skill is part of a chain (has next_chain and/or prev_chain), the overlay must show the full stacked sequence (e.g. Sword of Wrath -> Sword Arc -> Sword Wave). When a skill is not in a chain, behavior is unchanged (single tooltip). SCOPE: skills only. Depends on FEAT-001 (dataset must carry id/next_chain/prev_chain). This half cannot be compiled in this sandbox (MSVC/Windows-only, built in CI); verify by careful reading.
steps: In src/translation/skill_tooltips.h, add chain metadata to the SkillTooltip struct: an id field (e.g. long long id = 0 or std::optional<long long>) and next/prev chain ids (e.g. std::optional<long long> nextChain, prevChain). Keep the existing translated string fields unchanged. Update the doc comment.

In src/translation/skill_tooltips.h, add a second index to SkillTooltipStore keyed by skill id (e.g. std::unordered_map<long long, SkillTooltip> m_byId, or store tooltips once and keep an id->key map). Declare a new public method, e.g. `std::vector<SkillTooltip> lookupChain(const std::string& ocrLine) const;` that returns the full ordered chain (head to tail) when the matched skill is part of a chain, or a single-element vector with just the matched tooltip when it is not, or an empty vector when nothing matched. Document that ordering is head-to-tail.

In src/translation/skill_tooltips.cpp loadFromFile: parse the new fields from each skill JSON object defensively (id, next_chain, prev_chain may be integers or absent). Reuse the existing jsonStr/hasNumber-style defensive helpers or add a small numeric getter. Populate SkillTooltip.id/nextChain/prevChain. Build BOTH indexes: the existing normalize(name_en) map AND the id-keyed map. Keep the existing name-key behavior byte-for-byte for non-chain lookups.

In src/translation/skill_tooltips.cpp, implement lookupChain: first resolve the matched tooltip via the EXISTING lookup(ocrLine) logic (exact then word-boundary-contains) so name matching is unchanged. If the match has no id or has neither nextChain nor prevChain, return a single-element vector {matched}. Otherwise reconstruct the chain: walk prevChain backward via the id index to the head (the member with no prevChain, or until an id is missing from the index), then walk nextChain forward from the head via the id index, collecting each SkillTooltip in order. Guard against cycles/broken links with a visited-set and a sane max length (e.g. cap at 16) so a corrupt dataset can never loop forever. Mirror the reference algorithm added in FEAT-001 (reconstruct_chain).

In src/ocr/ocr_api.cpp, change the emit section (currently `auto tooltip = handle->translator.skillTooltips().lookup(line); if (tooltip.has_value()) { emit name/type/desc/notes/facts }`) to call lookupChain(line) instead. Iterate the returned vector and, for EACH tooltip in the chain, emit its name(kind 1)/type(kind 2)/description(kind 3)/notes(kind 4)/facts(kind 5) lines in order, exactly as the single-tooltip path does today. The existing kind-1 name header already renders a Separator before it in the overlay, so stacked chain members are visually separated. Preserve the BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS cap: emitLine already returns false / is guarded at the cap, so a long chain simply truncates safely without overflowing the caller array or dangling resultStorage pointers. Do not change the resultStorage reserve-before-loop logic. The fallback (no match -> single-line translate or raw line) path stays unchanged.

In src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp, raise the rendered displayLines cap (currently `if (displayLines.size() >= 40) break;`) so a multi-skill chain is not silently truncated below a full chain's worth of lines. Choose a cap consistent with BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS (96) so the overlay can show a realistic 2-3 skill chain in full; keep it bounded so the panel cannot grow unbounded. Keep the (lineKind + text) de-dup so repeated OCR frames still collapse but distinct chain members (distinct names/facts) are all shown.

Update the doc comment in src/ocr/ocr_api.h if the BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS rationale text should mention chains (a matched skill may now emit multiple stacked tooltips). Keep the numeric cap unless a chain of realistic length would not fit; if you change it, update both the macro and the comment and keep the overlay cap consistent.
acceptance_criteria: SkillTooltipStore exposes lookupChain returning an ordered head-to-tail vector<SkillTooltip>: full chain for chain members, single element for non-chain matches, empty for no match.
loadFromFile builds an id-keyed index in addition to the name-key index and parses id/next_chain/prev_chain defensively without throwing on missing/typed-wrong fields.
Chain reconstruction walks prev_chain to the head then next_chain forward, is cycle-safe (visited set + max length cap), and mirrors the FEAT-001 reference algorithm.

ocr_api.cpp emits the FULL chain's tooltip lines (name/type/description/notes/facts per member, in order) for a matched chain skill, and unchanged single-tooltip output for a non-chain skill, while never exceeding BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS or breaking the resultStorage pointer-lifetime invariant.
The overlay display-line cap is raised enough to show a realistic 2-3 skill chain without truncating a full chain, while remaining bounded.
Non-skill behavior and the no-match fallback path are unchanged; scope stays skills-only.
verification: This half is MSVC/Windows-only and cannot be compiled in this Linux sandbox. Verify by careful reading: (a) new struct fields and both indexes are declared and populated; (b) lookupChain reuses the existing lookup() for name matching and correctly walks prev->head->next with a cycle guard; (c) the ocr_api.cpp emit loop iterates the chain and every emitLine call remains guarded by the BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS cap with no change to the resultStorage.reserve-before-loop; (d) the overlay cap change is consistent with the result cap. Confirm no obvious C++ syntax/type errors (balanced braces, correct optional usage, no use-after-move).
Grep to confirm lookup() is no longer the only entry point used by ocr_api.cpp (lookupChain is called) and that the single-tooltip emit block was replaced by a per-member loop.
findings: Implemented the C++ consumer half. skill_tooltips.h: added id (long long id=0) + std::optional<long long> nextChain/prevChain to SkillTooltip, added m_byId (unordered_map<long long,SkillTooltip>) index and declared lookupChain(). skill_tooltips.cpp: added anonymous-namespace jsonInt() defensive integer getter (missing key -> nullopt, which correctly means non-chain); loadFromFile now parses id/next_chain/prev_chain and populates BOTH the existing normalize(name_en) map (byte-for-byte unchanged) and the new id index (only for nonzero ids; copies into m_byId before moving into m_tooltips, so no use-after-move); implemented lookupChain which reuses lookup() for name matching, returns {matched} for non-chain/old-dataset (id==0 or no next/prev), else walks prevChain back to head then nextChain forward, with visited-set cycle guards and a kMaxChainLen=16 cap, mirroring the Python reconstruct_chain. Added #include <unordered_set>. ocr_api.cpp: replaced the single lookup()+emit block with lookupChain(line) and a per-member loop emitting name(1)/type(2)/description(3)/notes(4)/facts(5) for each chain member in order; resultStorage reserve-before-loop and emitLine cap guard left untouched; fallback (no-match) branch unchanged. ocr_api.h: updated the BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS doc comment to note a matched skill may emit multiple stacked tooltips (a chain); numeric cap kept at 96 (fits a realistic 2-3 skill chain). imgui_overlay.cpp: raised the displayLines cap from 40 to 96 (consistent with BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS), keeping the (lineKind+text) de-dup. VERIFICATION: C++ is MSVC/Windows-only and cannot compile in this sandbox; verified by careful reading (fields+both indexes declared/populated, lookupChain reuses lookup() and is cycle-safe, works on OLD dataset as single tooltip, emit loop cap-guarded, overlay cap consistent, no use-after-move, balanced braces, correct optional usage). Grep confirms ocr_api.cpp now calls lookupChain (no bare lookup()) with a per-member loop. Python self-checks (the buildable gate) pass: python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --dry-run exits 0 with all checks OK including reconstruct_chain.
